default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1388.title: Opening gap fade on the first counter bar
E-1388.hypothesis: A session opening far from yesterday's close (relative to yesterday's range) is a thin-book jump; the first decisive bar back toward the prior close shows gap holders giving up, and the gap tends to be filled.

E-1389.title: Prior-close location bias entry
E-1389.hypothesis: When yesterday closed in the top (bottom) of its range, overnight holders carry that bias into the next session; a close back above (below) a short EMA in the first three hours is the entry in that direction.

E-1390.title: Rolling-window VWAP cross follow
E-1390.hypothesis: A volume-weighted average over only the last n minutes is the recent average cost; a close across it shows the latest participants changing from underwater to profitable (or the reverse) and they follow.

E-1391.title: Price-time correlation trend follow
E-1391.hypothesis: Correlation between price and time near +1 means an orderly staircase advance that slow participants keep chasing; follow the first bar where it crosses the threshold.

E-1392.title: Wick pressure accumulation follow
E-1392.hypothesis: Averaged over a window, long lower wicks and short upper wicks mean dips are repeatedly absorbed by resting buyers; trade with the absorbing side when the average crosses the threshold.

E-1393.title: Session-range midpoint recross follow
E-1393.hypothesis: The middle of today's high-low range is the balance point of the day's auction; after price spent a while on one side, a close through it shows the other side taking control.

E-1394.title: Volume acceleration direction follow
E-1394.hypothesis: Short-term average volume jumping well above the longer average shows urgent participation; the direction of price over that short window is the side that is urgent, and it keeps pushing.

E-1395.title: Return-skew rebound
E-1395.hypothesis: Strongly negative skew in recent returns means a few big down bars among small up bars, a liquidation profile; sellers are forced, not informed, and the price rebounds (mirror for positive skew).

E-1396.title: Up-bar share breadth follow
E-1396.hypothesis: When most recent bars close above their open the tape shows steady small buyers lifting offers; a share crossing the threshold marks a persistent one-sided flow that continues.

E-1397.title: Staircase higher-lows follow
E-1397.hypothesis: A window where most bars make a higher low (or lower high) shows dips bought a little higher each time; pullback buyers are stepping up and the stair continues.
